375093.title: Artemev's singular-part conjecture for dual topological-recursion amplitudes
375093.statement:
Let $A^{(g),\vee}_n(k_1,\dots,k_n)$ be the amplitudes obtained from topological recursion after applying the $x-y$ swap to the minimal-string spectral curve, and let $A^{(g),\mathsf{sing}}_n(k_1,\dots,k_n)$ denote the singular-in-$u^2$ part of the original amplitudes. Here $g\geq 0$, $n\geq 1$, and $k_1,\dots,k_n\in\{1,\dots,p\}$.

**Artemev's conjecture.** Up to a suitable normalization, $A^{(g),\vee}_n(k_1,\dots,k_n)$ coincides with $A^{(g),\mathsf{sing}}_n(k_1,\dots,k_n)$ for $g\geq 0$, $n\geq 1$, and $k_1,\dots,k_n=1,\dots,p$.

This is the amplitude-level formulation of the resonance-transformation claim after the $x-y$ swap. The paper presents a proof of Artemev's conjecture, so the stated identification is resolved.

375205.title: Hegedüs's balanced Sperner family conjecture
375205.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\dots,n\}$. A family $\mathcal{F}\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ is **Sperner** if no two distinct members are comparable under inclusion. It is **$2$-balanced** if there are pairwise disjoint nonempty sets $I_1,I_2\subseteq[m]$, where $\mathcal{F}=\{F_1,\dots,F_m\}$, such that

$$
\bigcup_{i\in I_1}F_i=\bigcup_{i\in I_2}F_i
$$

and

$$
\bigcap_{i\in I_1}F_i=\bigcap_{i\in I_2}F_i.
$$

**Hegedüs's conjecture.** If $\mathcal{F}\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ is a Sperner family and $|\mathcal{F}|\ge n+1$, then $\mathcal{F}$ is $2$-balanced.

The conjecture was proposed after Hegedüs proved the corresponding statement for uniform families. The supplied abstract states that the result for $r=2$ has been proved with the sharp threshold $n+1$, so this conjecture is solved.

375277.title: The one-point extension conjecture for Euclidean Ramsey sets
375277.statement:
Let $X\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a finite **Ramsey** set, and regard $\mathbb R^d$ as a hyperplane in $\mathbb R^{d+1}$. Let $z\in\mathbb R^{d+1}$ be a point outside that hyperplane.

**One-point extension conjecture.** The set $X\cup\{z\}$ is Ramsey.

The paper calls this an intriguing open problem. It would follow from either of the two competing conjectures that Ramsey sets are exactly the spherical sets or exactly the subtransitive sets.

375522.title: Perfect-power maximality conjecture for periodic grid quotients
375522.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and $n\ge3$. Let $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{Z}^d$ be a full-rank sublattice, let $S\subset\mathbb{Z}^d$ be $\Lambda$-periodic, and let $\mathcal L_d[S]/\Lambda$ be the corresponding finite simple quotient graph. Suppose this quotient is connected and has $n^d$ vertex orbits.

**Periodic perfect-power maximality conjecture.** Its spanning-tree count is at most

$$
\tau(\mathcal L_d[S]/\Lambda)\le \tau(C_n^{\square d}).
$$

Equality should occur only for the standard product torus $C_n^{\square d}$, up to the natural quotient symmetries. The conjecture extends the comparison for rectangular tori to general periodic grid quotients, but the appropriate ambient class is less canonical than the class of connected induced subgraphs of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, so this remains open.

375561.title: The upper bound on the strong periodicity of connected graphs under the 2-distance operator
375561.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be any connected graph, and let $\rho^2(G)$ denote its strong periodicity under the 2-distance operator.

**Upper-bound conjecture.** Any connected graph $G=(V,E)$ has

$$
\rho^2(G)\leq |V|-3.
$$

This conjecture gives a universal linear upper bound on the strong periodicity of connected graphs under the 2-distance operator. The supplied text does not state whether the bound has been proved or refuted.

375685.title: Ohba's chromatic-choosability conjecture
375685.statement: For a graph $G$, let $\chi(G)$ be its chromatic number, and let $\chi_\ell(G)$ be its list chromatic number. A graph is **chromatic-choosable** when $\chi_\ell(G)=\chi(G)$. **Ohba's conjecture.** Any graph $G$ with at most $2\chi(G)+1$ vertices is chromatic-choosable. The supplied text says this conjecture was proved by Noel et al.; the bound is tight, since examples with $2\chi(G)+2$ vertices are not chromatic-choosable.

375704.title: Injective edge-function conjecture for length-area transferal
375704.statement: Let $G=(\mathcal{V},\mathcal{E})$ be a simplicial complex. A **triangle edge choice function** assigns to each triangle of $G$ one of its edges, and it is **injective** when distinct triangles are assigned distinct edges. **Injective edge-function conjecture.** Length-area transferal holds for $G$ if and only if there exists an injective triangle edge choice function. The authors know no simplicial complex with an injective edge choice function for which length-area transferal fails; the conjecture therefore proposes that injectivity is sufficient, while the stated equivalence remains open.

375777.title: Ellis–Keller–Lifshitz stability conjecture for intersecting families
375777.statement:
Let $n$, $k$, $t$, and $d$ satisfy

$$
n\geq(t+1)(k-t+1),\qquad d\in\mathbb{N}.
$$

Let $\mathcal{F}\subseteq\binom{[n]}{k}$ be $t$-intersecting. **Ellis–Keller–Lifshitz stability conjecture.** If

$$
|\mathcal{F}|\geq\max\left\{(t+2)\binom{n-t-2}{k-t-1}-(t+1)\binom{n-t-2}{k-t-2},
\binom{n-t}{k-t}-\binom{n-t-d}{k-t}+t\binom{n-t-d}{k-t-d+1}\right\},
$$

then there exists a $t$-subset $X$ such that

$$
|\mathcal{F}\setminus\mathcal{F}[X]|\leq t\binom{n-t-d}{k-t-d+1}.
$$

Here $\mathcal{F}[X]$ denotes the subfamily of members of $\mathcal{F}$ containing $X$. The conjecture was proposed by Ellis, Keller and Lifshitz as a strengthening of their stability theorem for $t$-intersecting families. The supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.

375850.title: The $7/5$ cycle-cover conjecture for bridgeless graphs
375850.statement:
Let $G$ be a bridgeless graph, not necessarily cubic, and let $E$ denote its edge set. A **cycle cover** here is a list of cycles in which every edge of $G$ lies on at least one cycle. **$7/5$ cycle-cover conjecture.** The graph $G$ has a list of cycles such that every edge lies on at least one of them and the sum of their lengths is at most

$$
\frac{7}{5}\cdot |E|.
$$

This is another classical conjecture listed as a consequence of the Petersen coloring conjecture. The source gives no evidence that it has been resolved.

376070.title: Ostmann's inverse Goldbach conjecture
376070.statement:
Let $\mathscr P$ denote the set of all primes. For sets $S,T$ of positive integers, define $S\sim T$ to mean that their symmetric difference is finite. **Ostmann's inverse Goldbach conjecture.** There do not exist sets $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ of positive integers, each with at least two elements, such that

$$
\mathscr P\sim \mathcal A+\mathcal B.
$$

This is the inverse form of the Goldbach problem: it asks whether the primes can be, up to finitely many exceptions, represented as the sumset of two nontrivial sets. The source presents it as an important motivation for the paired inverse large sieve conjecture; its resolution status is not specified in the supplied text.

376096.title: The orientable 5-cycle double cover conjecture
376096.statement:
An **orientable cycle double cover** of a graph $G$ is a list of Eulerian subgraphs, each equipped with a directed Eulerian orientation, such that every edge of $G$ is used exactly once in each direction. An **orientable $k$-cycle double cover** is an orientable cycle double cover with at most $k$ Eulerian subgraphs.

**Orientable 5-cycle double cover conjecture.** Every bridgeless graph admits an orientable $5$-cycle double cover.

The conjecture would imply Tutte's $5$-flow conjecture. The source gives this implication but no resolution of the orientable cover conjecture.

376097.title: The 5-cycle double cover conjecture for graphic matroids
376097.statement:
A **graphic matroid** is the cycle matroid of a graph. A **coloop** is an element belonging to every basis, and a **$k$-cycle double cover** of a matroid is a family of at most $k$ cycles such that every element belongs to exactly two members.

**Graphic matroid 5-cycle double cover conjecture.** Every graphic matroid without coloops has a $5$-cycle double cover.

This is the matroid formulation of the graph-theoretic $5$-cycle double cover conjecture. The source establishes an eight-cycle bound for graphic matroids without coloops but leaves the five-cycle bound open.

376179.title: Conjecture on dense colorings for typical norms
376179.statement:
For a norm $\|\cdot\|$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, write $\chi(\mathbb{R}^n;\|\cdot\|)$ for the chromatic number of its unit-distance graph, and let $\chi_{ed}(\mathbb{R}^n;\|\cdot\|)$ denote the least number of color classes in a proper coloring whose classes are dense in $\mathbb{R}^n$. A norm is called **typical** if it belongs to the Baire-category typical set in the space of norms.

**Typical-norm dense-coloring conjecture.** For a typical norm,

$$
\chi_{ed}\bigl(\mathbb{R}^n;\|\cdot\|\bigr)=\chi\bigl(\mathbb{R}^n;\|\cdot\|\bigr)=2^n.
$$

For typical norms, the equality $\chi(\mathbb{R}^n;\|\cdot\|)=2^n$ is known, but the coloring establishing it is nonconstructive. The conjecture asserts that requiring every color class to be dense does not increase the chromatic number.

376183.title: Rapaport–Strasser conjecture for Hamilton cycles in connected Cayley graphs
376183.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite group and let $S\subseteq\Gamma\setminus\{1\}$ satisfy $S=S^{-1}$. The Cayley graph $\operatorname{Cay}(\Gamma,S)$ has vertex set $\Gamma$ and edges $\{g,gs\}$ for $g\in\Gamma$ and $s\in S$; assume it is connected, equivalently, that $S$ generates $\Gamma$. A Hamilton cycle is a cycle containing every vertex of the graph.

**Rapaport–Strasser conjecture.** Every connected Cayley graph on a finite group with at least three elements has a Hamilton cycle.

The conjecture is known for finite abelian groups and for several dense classes of Cayley graphs, but the full conjecture remains open.

376276.title: Hušek–Šámal's exponential circuit double cover conjecture
376276.statement:
Let $G$ be a $2$-connected cubic graph on $n$ vertices. A **circuit double cover** (CiDC) is a finite family of connected $2$-regular subgraphs of $G$ such that every edge belongs to exactly two members of the family.

**Hušek–Šámal's conjecture.** The graph $G$ has at least

$$
2^{n/2-1}
$$

CiDCs.

This is a quantitative strengthening of the cycle double cover problem. The bound is proved in the source for $2$-connected $3$-edge-colorable cubic graphs and is known to be tight for Klee graphs, while the general conjecture remains open.

376277.title: The five-cycle double cover conjecture
376277.statement:
Let $G$ be a bridgeless cubic graph. A **$5$-cycle double cover** ($5$-CyDC) is a tuple of five cycles of $G$ such that every edge belongs to exactly two members of the tuple.

**Five-cycle double cover conjecture.** Every bridgeless cubic graph has a $5$-CyDC.

The ordinary cycle double cover conjecture is stated in the source as solved, but the five-cycle version remains open. The paper also gives a flow-only formulation of this conjecture and proves related results, including a characterization for a prescribed cycle.

376299.title: Hoàng's conjecture on bisimplicial vertices in minimally nonperfectly divisible graphs
376299.statement: All graphs considered are finite and simple. For a graph $G$, write $\rho(G)$ for its chromatic number and $\tau(G)$ for its clique number. A graph is **minimally nonperfectly divisible** (MNPD) if it is not perfectly divisible, while every proper induced subgraph is perfectly divisible. A vertex is **bisimplicial** if its neighbourhood is the union of two cliques. **Hoàng's conjecture.** No MNPD graph contains a bisimplicial vertex. The paper disproves this conjecture by constructing an explicit infinite family of MNPD graphs with a bisimplicial vertex.

376344.title: Six-connectivity conjecture for rigidity of K4-covered graphs
376344.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph that is **6-connected** (it remains connected after deletion of any set of at most five vertices) and **$K_4$-covered** (every edge lies in a copy of $K_4$).

**Six-connectivity conjecture.** Every 6-connected $K_4$-covered graph is rigid in $\mathbb{R}^3$.

The paper proves rigidity under the stronger hypothesis of 5-connectivity together with $\mathcal{R}$-bridgelessness, and notes that the analogous cofactor statement is known. The conjecture would be false with 5-connectivity in place of 6-connectivity, so the stated bound is the proposed improvement.

376345.title: Six-connectivity conjecture for global rigidity of 3-dimensional combinatorial zeolites
376345.statement:
A **3-dimensional combinatorial zeolite** is the line graph of a 4-regular graph. Let $G$ be such a graph, and suppose that $G$ is **6-connected**, meaning that deletion of any set of at most five vertices leaves it connected.

**Combinatorial-zeolite conjecture.** Every 6-connected 3-dimensional combinatorial zeolite is globally rigid in $\mathbb{R}^3$.

The source motivates this by the analogous two-dimensional result, where 3-connected combinatorial zeolites are globally rigid in $\mathbb{R}^2$. It also notes that a stronger 4-connectivity conjecture was posed by others; the 6-connectivity statement remains open in the supplied text.

376357.title: The extremal arc-count conjecture for strongly connected digraphs without acyclic separators
376357.statement:
Let $D$ be a strongly connected digraph with $n\geq 3$ vertices and $m$ arcs. An **acyclic separator** is a separator whose induced subdigraph is acyclic. **Extremal arc-count conjecture.** If $D$ does not have an acyclic separator, then

$$
m\geq 3n-3.
$$

The digraph $\vec{C}_n^*$ described in the surrounding text has $3(n-1)=3n-3$ arcs and is strongly $2$-connected, neighborhood-cyclic, and has no acyclic separator, motivating the claimed sharp lower bound.
